_comment: Figure manifest for the Axial SWS site. 'source' is repo-relative and is READ ONLY - build_figures.py never modifies, moves, or commits source files. 'page' is 1-indexed. 'width' overrides defaults.width for dense multi-panel figures. 'badge' marks a figure that predates the Grade-3/windowcheck pipeline so it is never silently shown as current.

pre_windowcheck.label: PRE-WINDOWCHECK
pre_windowcheck.tooltip: Generated before the 2026-07-24 undersized-window fix. Not from the current Grade-3 production chain.

partial_stations.label: 3 OF 6 STATIONS
partial_stations.tooltip: Pools AXCC1 + AXEC1 + AXEC2 only. A six-station regeneration is pending.

older_inversion.label: OLDER RUN
older_inversion.tooltip: From the July 2026 raw-quality inversion, not the Grade-3 windowcheck run. Shown because no Grade-3 checkerboard was produced.

stale_threshold.label: THRESHOLD OUT OF DATE
stale_threshold.tooltip: Diagram shows Q_w ≥ 0.5; production Grade 3 is Q_w ≥ 0.75. Needs redrawing.

degenerate_fit.label: FIT DEGENERATE
degenerate_fit.tooltip: The fitted inflation azimuth collapses onto the fixed background azimuth and A blows up, producing a discontinuity. Read the scatter, not the curve.

beta_unconstrained.label: β NOT CONSTRAINED
beta_unconstrained.tooltip: With α fixed and C1, C2 free, the atan2 vector-sum model reduces exactly to a 3-parameter arctangent, so the inflation azimuth β is not identifiable from φ-vs-uplift data (profile likelihood flat over 222–356° of 360°). Read the curve, not β.

figures.title: Geological structure of Axial Seamount
figures.caption: Caldera setting over shaded bathymetry. White dotted line: outline of the main magma reservoir (MMR); orange and red contours: the MMR roof at 1.5 km and 1.25 km depth. Hatched grey polygons: the east and west ring faults. Black lines: rift zones and dikes, running north and south from the caldera. Green outlines: the 2015 lava flows. Stations are coloured by instrument — yellow for short-period (AS1, AS2, EC1, EC3), blue for broadband (CC1, EC2). The Pacific–Juan de Fuca plate boundary runs through the caldera.

figures.title: Caldera setting and relocated seismicity
figures.caption: Axial Seamount caldera. Native-colour bathymetry, every processed event in the MLdd catalog (deduplicated by origin time across the six stations), and the six OOI Regional Cabled Array OBS stations.

figures.title: Measurement distributions (1/5)
figures.caption: Distributions of every numeric output column: φ, δt, their errors, Q_w, SNR, rectilinearity, incidence, dominant period, and the per-event chosen filter band.

figures.title: Quality vs. source depth
figures.caption: Log-count 2-D histograms of Q_w against source depth, one panel per station. No Q_w cut applied — Q_w is the axis.

figures.title: Back-azimuth, depth & quality — AXAS1
figures.caption: Back-azimuth against source depth and against Q_w. Baseline cleanup only, so the full Q_w < 0 null population stays visible — this is the panel that tests the Wüstefeld (2010) prediction that true nulls cluster at discrete back-azimuths while false nulls scatter.

figures.title: Splitting measurement pipeline
figures.caption: End-to-end workflow: waveform retrieval and QC, dominant-period estimation, MFAST-style dynamic windowing, LQT rotation on the PyKonal-traced S incidence, Silver & Chan eigenvalue minimisation over the window/lag/angle grid, and DBSCAN clustering with Teanby (2004) representative-variance selection. Note: the "Final Filtering" box in this diagram gives Q_w ≥ 0.5 as its example threshold; the production Grade-3 cut is Q_w ≥ 0.75. The diagram's text is baked into vector glyph paths and it has no generating script, so correcting it means rebuilding the figure by hand.

figures.title: A well-constrained split
figures.caption: AXEC2, event 298_74456, 2015-04-21. Q_w = 1.000, SNR = 23.3, rectilinearity = 0.999, incidence = 14.6°, φ_err = 7°, δt = 0.03 ± 0.005 s. The highest-ranked measurement across all 497 pre-eruption batches.

figures.title: A well-constrained null
figures.caption: AXEC2, event 74_18279, 2015-03-02. Q_w = −0.984, at the discretised floor — the most confident 'no splitting' the metric can express. δt = 0.01 s with δt_err = 0.005 s, so the null is not confounded by a noisy measurement.

figures.title: Cycle skipping
figures.caption: AXEC2, event 238_59346, 2015-04-06. Q_w = 0.000 (indeterminate), δt = 0.16 s against T_dom/2 = 0.0345 s — 4.6× over threshold, with a broad non-unique error-surface minimum. This is the case that motivates the δt ≤ T_dom/2 cut in the Grade-3 filter.

figures.title: Fast direction by eruption-relative period
figures.caption: Six station rows × seven periods (before, during, and five equal-event-count post-eruption bins), grouped by western and eastern caldera. Each panel carries N, mean φ ± SE, and the axial cosine similarity to that station's pre-eruption panel.

figures.title: Roses on the caldera map — 5 equal-inflation periods
figures.caption: Grade-3 fast-direction roses at each station for the five post-eruption periods that carry equal amounts of Central Caldera uplift, on low-contrast bathymetry showing the full caldera rim; the sixth panel shows the uplift curve with the periods shaded. AXEC2 and AXEC3 sit only 0.54 km apart, so at this rose size their roses are nudged apart with leader lines to their true positions. AXEC2's unlevelled 2021-07 to 2022-09 window is excluded.

figures.title: Fast direction by equal-inflation period
figures.caption: The same figure with the five post-eruption bins carrying equal amounts of Central Caldera inflation rather than equal event counts — the physically motivated companion, and the newest of the rose set.

figures.title: Fast direction by year
figures.caption: Fourteen annual columns: pre-2015, syn-2015, post-2015, then 2016 through 2026.

figures.title: Back-azimuth decomposition, by period
figures.caption: Each cell's central rose ringed by six 60° back-azimuth sub-roses, testing whether the fast direction is a back-azimuth sampling artefact rather than a property of the medium.

figures.title: AXAS1 — equal-inflation periods
figures.caption: Western caldera (ASHES). Post-eruption bins carry equal physical inflation. AXAS1 and AXAS2 reference the ASHES BOTPT, whose record begins 2017-08-15.

figures.title: AXCC1 — equal-inflation periods
figures.caption: Central caldera. No real data exists 2015-03-01 to 2015-04-28 — the sensor was unlevelled by pre-eruption inflation and reset after eruption onset.

figures.title: Percent anisotropy vs. uplift — pre- and syn-eruption
figures.caption: Percent anisotropy A = δt / T_S × 100 against de-tided Central Caldera uplift before and during the eruption. Pre-eruption runs from the start of the record (2015-01-22) to the uplift peak, taken at eruption onset (2015-04-24 06:00); syn-eruption runs from that peak to the post-eruption uplift minimum (2015-05-02), the zero reference of every post-eruption figure. Pre-eruption uplift is relative to that minimum (positive, 5-day rolling); syn-eruption uplift is relative to the peak (mean of the 24 h before onset), so it is negative: 0 → −2.4 m of deflation. Syn values are daily (the period is 9 days), with ±1 SE from that day's events. Linear trendline on every series. Read the syn trends with care: most of the deflation happens within the first day, so the onset day (−1.55 m) is the only point away from the −2.3 to −2.4 m cluster and it sets the slopes. AXCC1 has no data 2015-03-01 → 04-28. 2015-05-03 → 05-18 (earliest re-inflation) is in neither this figure nor the post-eruption ones, which start at 05-19.

figures.title: Fast direction vs. uplift — pre- and syn-eruption
figures.caption: Same periods, uplift references, smoothing and layout as the percent-anisotropy figure, for the circular-mean fast direction (one y-axis wrap per column so rows line up). Linear trendlines only — the atan2 fit cannot be constrained by 9 days, and its β is not identifiable anyway. The same onset-day leverage applies to the syn trends; pre-eruption AXCC1 is bimodal, so its trendline does not describe it, and AXCC1's syn panel spans only 0.04 m of uplift, so its slope is not a physical rate.

figures.title: Percent anisotropy vs. uplift — post-eruption, with trendlines
figures.caption: A = δt / T_S × 100 with T_S read directly from the PyKonal eikonal travel-time field through the Baillard 3-D S-velocity model. Normalising by T_S tests whether the δt trends are a ray-path-length effect: each panel lists r with uplift for δt, A and T_S. The West increase is genuine anisotropy (T_S flat; A slopes +0.57 / +1.21 %/m at AXAS1 / AXAS2, +0.84 %/m West average); AXCC1's weak δt rise is path-length driven (r(T_S, u) = +0.45, A slightly falls); the East is flat to slightly falling (−0.17 %/m). AXEC2 2015–2021 hypocentres were filled from the raw-batch metadata (its windowcheck CSV carries none).

figures.title: West · Central · East — φ vs. uplift, station and regional atan2 fits
figures.caption: Top row: every station on its own, 50% opacity, each with its own atan2 vector-sum fit (IBM colour-blind-safe palette — West: AXAS1 orange, AXAS2 blue; East: AXEC1 purple, AXEC2 magenta, AXEC3 gold; regional average black); Central shows AXCC1 in dark green. Bottom row: the regional averages (black) with their atan2 fits — the same fits as the single-region pages (West β = 125.2°, r = 0.52; East β = 247.3°, r = 0.69). Each column shares one y-axis wrap, so the rows line up. Light vertical bars are ±1 standard error of each rolling circular mean. A '(degenerate)' legend tag marks fits where β collapses onto the fixed background azimuth α (parallel or antiparallel) or A > 10: AXCC1, and all three East stations (AXEC1 β = 350°, AXEC2 β = 170°, AXEC3 β = 169.7°, A = 12–23). Those curves are effectively free S-curves and describe the shape well (AXEC2 r = 0.84), but their inflation azimuths mean nothing. Station fits drop AXEC2's unlevelled window, so they differ from the per-station atan2 pages, which flag it instead.

figures.title: Delay time vs. uplift — post-eruption
figures.caption: 30-day rolling mean δt against uplift, stations on top and regional averages below, shared δt axis, ±1 SE bars. δt rises with uplift in the West (AXAS1 r = +0.60, AXAS2 +0.51) and is flat to slightly falling in the East. See the percent-anisotropy version above for the path-length-normalised view.

figures.title: West · Central · East — φ vs. uplift, data only
figures.caption: The same three regional series with no model at all: just the rolling mean fast direction against uplift, and a light ±1 SE bar on every point. Each panel keeps its own wrap so its cloud never splits across the 0/180° edge, so equal heights in different panels are not equal angles. N = 2209 (West), 1303 (Central), 3064 (East); AXEC2's unlevelled 2021-07 to 2022-09 window is excluded from East. Individual member stations sit underneath at 50% opacity (IBM colour-blind-safe palette — West: AXAS1 orange, AXAS2 blue; East: AXEC1 purple, AXEC2 magenta, AXEC3 gold; regional average black), each rolled the same way as the average.

figures.title: Change in φ since re-inflation began — West · Central · East
figures.caption: Δφ relative to each region's circular-mean φ in the first 30 days after the eruption (from 2015-05-19), on one shared y-axis. Because φ is axial, the axis cycles mod 180°; the shared 180° window (centred at −51°) is chosen automatically to keep every region's cloud away from the edges (≤ 1.7% of points within 15° of an edge). Ticks beyond ±90° are the equivalent orientation (−120° ≡ +60°). Light bars are ±1 SE of the rolling mean. All three regions rotate counter-clockwise with re-inflation — East by ~25–30°, West by ~90° — but West's reference rests on only 14 events (75° ± 10°), so its offset is loosely constrained. Individual member stations sit underneath at 50% opacity (IBM colour-blind-safe palette — West: AXAS1 orange, AXAS2 blue; East: AXEC1 purple, AXEC2 magenta, AXEC3 gold; regional average black), each rolled the same way as the average and referenced to its REGION's φ_ref, so station offsets are real orientation differences. Note AXEC2 diverging to ≈ −60° above 1.7 m while AXEC1 stays near +10°.

figures.title: Regional mean φ vs. uplift — Western Caldera
figures.caption: AXAS1 + AXAS2 pooled into a single western-caldera mean fast direction, against the same Central Caldera BOTPT uplift. Measurements are collapsed to per-calendar-day circular means before the 30-day roll, so each day counts once for the region. Fitted inflation azimuth β = 125.2°, A = 1.02, r = 0.52 over N = 2209. Note the turnover is auto-estimated at u₀ = 0.05 m, i.e. pinned to the low edge of the uplift range, so the fitted curve is a decay across the observed span rather than a completed S-transition.

figures.title: Regional mean φ vs. uplift — Eastern Caldera
figures.caption: AXEC1 + AXEC2 + AXEC3 pooled into an eastern-caldera mean, against Central Caldera uplift. The cleanest of the three regional fits: a steady rotation from about 160° to 130° with β = 247.3°, A = 1.27, r = 0.69 over N = 3064. AXEC2's 2021-07 to 2022-09 unlevelled window (520 measurements) is dropped from the pool rather than flagged, since a known instrumental drift would otherwise pull the regional average. The turnover sits at u₀ = 2.63 m, the upper edge of the observed uplift, so this span samples the near-linear part of the curve.

figures.title: Regional mean φ vs. uplift — Central Caldera
figures.caption: AXCC1 alone, against the Central Caldera uplift it sits on. The scatter is real and shows a rotation with inflation, but THE FITTED CURVE SHOULD NOT BE READ AS A RESULT: the fit returns β = 170.0°, exactly the fixed background azimuth α = 170°, with A = 41.7 against 0.4–1.3 at every other station or region. With β collapsed onto α the two stress vectors are collinear, the vector sum degenerates, and the atan2 argument flips sign across the turnover — which is the vertical jump visible at u₀ = 1.03 m. This is the same failure mode noted for AXCC1 in inflation_vector_map_sixstations_ccal.py, and it needs resolving before AXCC1's inflation-vector azimuth is used for anything.

figures.title: Uplift vs. fast direction — AXAS1
figures.caption: φ against Central Caldera uplift, matched 30-day rolling windows on both axes, fitted with the atan2 vector-sum model: a fixed regional tectonic stress vector plus a fixed-orientation inflation vector whose magnitude grows with uplift. Turnover u0 is auto-estimated per station by a free-location logistic pre-fit.

figures.title: Uplift vs. fast direction — AXCC1
figures.caption: AXCC1's fit returns A ≈ 42 against 0.4–20 at every other station, producing a near-discontinuous rather than smooth transition. Treat this fit, and the AXCC1 arrow on the inflation-vector map, with more caution than the other five.

figures.title: Fitted inflation-vector azimuths
figures.caption: Grayscale bathymetry with each station's fitted inflation-vector azimuth β as a red arrow. Reuses compute_all_station_fits() from the fit above, so the map cannot drift from the fits. AXCC1's arrow inherits the caveat noted on its panel.

figures.title: Uplift vs. φ, unfitted — AXAS1
figures.caption: The deliberate no-fit view: pre-eruption deflation and post-eruption re-inflation as two panels pivoting at zero uplift, 90-day windows. Complementary to the fitted version, not superseded by it.

figures.title: Central Caldera BOTPT — de-tided depth and uplift
figures.caption: De-tided seafloor depth 2015-01-22 to 2026-05-15, and metres of uplift referenced to the post-eruption minimum, with the five equal-inflation period boundaries marked. Total re-inflation ≈ 2.6 m.

figures.title: ASHES BOTPT — de-tided depth and uplift
figures.caption: The western-caldera geodetic reference used by AXAS1 and AXAS2. Record begins 2017-08-15.

figures.title: Which function fits? — Western Caldera
figures.caption: Fifteen candidate families fitted to the same western regional φ-vs-uplift data and ranked by AICc: linear, quadratic, cubic, logarithmic, square root, cube root, power law, exponential decay and saturation, hyperbolic, logistic, tanh, arctangent, erfc, and the production atan2 vector-sum. NO FORM IS SUPPORTED HERE — R² is 0.13–0.16 on the thinned series and the whole 15-model field spans only ΔAICc 7.2, so nothing is distinguishable. The atan2 model ranks last of fifteen on the thinned series.

figures.title: Which function fits? — Eastern Caldera
figures.caption: Same battery on the eastern regional mean, where a real relationship does exist (R² ≈ 0.48 daily, 0.35 thinned). Its SHAPE is not resolved: arctangent wins on the raw series but plain LINEAR wins once the series is decimated to ~independent samples, with eleven of fifteen models inside ΔAICc 2.3 of each other. The fitted curves overlay almost exactly across the observed uplift range. The atan2 vector-sum model ranks 8th raw and 12th thinned. Median residual lag-1 ρ = 0.948, so effective N ≈ 82 of 3064 — which is why the raw ranking cannot be taken at face value.

figures.title: Which function fits? — AXAS1
figures.caption: Thinned winner: logarithmic. atan2 ranks 15/15 (ΔAICc 5.7) despite an R² of 0.292 against the winner's 0.288 — it fits marginally BETTER and loses purely on the k=5 penalty.

figures.title: Which function fits? — AXAS2
figures.caption: Essentially no relationship to fit: R² = 0.040. Whatever ranks first here is ranking noise. Consistent with AXAS2 being the station that does not show the eruption-onset response its western neighbour AXAS1 does.

figures.title: Which function fits? — AXCC1
figures.caption: Thinned winner: logistic, with atan2 ranked 5/15 at ΔAICc 0.6 — statistically tied for best, and the highest R² of any model here (0.326 vs 0.317). Note this is about GOODNESS OF FIT only: AXCC1's atan2 PARAMETERS are separately degenerate (β collapses onto α, A ≈ 42), so a good fit here does not rescue its inflation-vector azimuth.

figures.title: Which function fits? — AXEC1
figures.caption: Thinned winner: erfc, atan2 6/15 at ΔAICc 3.9. Four models tie within ΔAICc 2.

figures.title: Which function fits? — AXEC2
figures.caption: The strongest relationship in the dataset — R² = 0.71 raw, 0.50 thinned — and the only station where raw and thinned rankings AGREE (cubic both times). Read the curves, not the ranking: logistic, tanh, erfc, arctangent and atan2 all trace the same S-curve and sit within ΔAICc 3.6 of each other on the thinned series, while the winning cubic bends UPWARD at low uplift where no data supports it — a polynomial edge artifact, not a physical form.

figures.title: Which function fits? — AXEC3
figures.caption: Thinned winner: cube root, atan2 15/15 (ΔAICc 7.2), R² 0.179 — a weak relationship.

figures.title: Is the inflation azimuth β constrained? Profile likelihood
figures.caption: β fixed on a 2° grid over the full circle, C1, C2 and A refit at each value, Δχ² corrected for the strong autocorrelation of the rolled series (effective N). For 7 of 8 series the profile is flat at Δχ² ≈ 0 over 222–356° of 360°; AXCC1's apparently constrained 50° is the degenerate collinear (β ≈ α) step. The reason is structural, not a data problem: with α fixed and C1, C2 free, the model reduces exactly to φ = C1′ + C2·atan((u − u₀)/w) with w = A²|sin(α − β)| — a 3-parameter arctangent reproduces the atan2 misfit to 1.0000 for 6 of 8 series. Fitted β values (and the inflation-vector map) therefore carry no information from these data.

figures.title: Are there periodic oscillations about the fits? Periodogram
figures.caption: Lomb–Scargle periodogram of the daily φ residual about each atan2 fit (sin 2r, wrap-safe), tested against an AR(1) red-noise null with a band-wide (global) 95% threshold. No significant peak in any series — nothing at annual, semi-annual or tidal (Mf, Mm) periods. Injection tests: a steady sinusoid at 14 d – 1 yr would be detected 90% of the time at ≥ 3–5° (East), 7–8° (West), 12–15° (AXAS2, AXCC1). The visible wiggles in the 30-day rolled plots are ~60–80% smoothing of day-to-day noise; the remainder is aperiodic, low-frequency wander.

figures.title: Transient oscillations? Wavelet scalograms
figures.caption: Morlet wavelet power of the same daily residuals (Torrence & Compo 1998), cone of influence and < 50%-coverage cells masked. A significant patch counts only if it lasts longer than 95% of the largest patches in AR(1) surrogates run through the identical pipeline (area-wise test). No patch passes in any of the 8 series; the pointwise-significant fraction (0.7–4.8%) is at or below the ~5% expected from noise.

figures.title: PCA of φ, δt and uplift — within and across stations
figures.caption: 30-day post-eruption bins, standardised variables, moving-block bootstrap. Network PC1 (30%; 25% after linear detrending) combines uplift (−0.95), φ at the East stations and δt with OPPOSITE signs west and east (AXAS1 −0.69, AXEC2 +0.58); PC2 is not robust. De-tided and raw uplift are redundant at this bin size (r ≥ 0.999). Unlike the circular statistics below, φ enters linearly on each station's own 180° branch; AXAS1 and AXCC1 span nearly 180°, so their φ loadings depend on where that branch is cut.

figures.title: Cross-correlation of φ, δt and uplift — levels, changes and lags
figures.caption: Same 14 variables and bins as the PCA. (a) Levels: 34 / 91 pairs significant after an effective-N correction, mostly shared secular trend. (b) 30-day changes: 9 / 91 (≈ 4.5 expected by chance); no seismic variable's change tracks the uplift change, though φ changes co-vary between stations (AXAS1–AXEC1 +0.43), possibly because the same events are seen at several stations. (c, d) Lagged cross-correlation of changes vs uplift change, ±1 yr: no consistent lead or lag. φ is treated linearly per station (see the PCA caveat).

figures.title: Correlation matrices — post-eruption, daily
figures.caption: Every station's rolling φ and δt against every other station's and against Central Caldera BOTPT uplift. Three different coefficients, not interchangeable: φ–φ uses the Jammalamadaka–Sarma circular-circular correlation on doubled (axial) angles; δt–δt and δt–uplift use Pearson; φ–δt and φ–uplift use the circular-linear R, which is UNSIGNED (0–1) and must not be read as if high meant positive. Pearson on raw φ would be wrong — it would treat 179° and 1° as maximally different. This page is daily-sampled and therefore autocorrelated; its significance is overstated.

figures.title: Correlation matrices — post-eruption, thinned
figures.caption: The same matrices decimated to one point per 30 days, roughly the decorrelation scale — believe this page where it disagrees with the daily one. Strongest station-station φ coupling is AXAS1–AXEC2 (r = 0.67), then AXCC1–AXEC3 (0.54). Against uplift, φ at AXAS1 (R = 0.79), AXEC2 (0.72) and AXCC1 (0.65) track the geodetic record most closely; δt tracks it far more weakly except at AXAS1 (0.58). Median pairwise N = 51.

figures.title: Correlation matrices — full record, thinned
figures.caption: The same matrices over the full record including the 2015 eruption. Station-station values here are inflated by the shared eruption-step response — every station responds to the same event, which registers as covariation whether or not the stations are otherwise coupled. Useful for seeing which stations respond in step; not a measure of ongoing coupling. AXEC2's unlevelled window is dropped throughout, and AXCC1's 2015-03-01 to 2015-04-28 gap is simply absent.

figures.title: Delay time through the eruption — AXEC2
figures.caption: δt as a moving-window density against time, with a ±48 h eruption zoom. Filtered Q_w > 0.5, φ_err < 20°, δt_err < 0.04 s. No Grade-3 equivalent of this figure exists yet — see the note below.

Fractional anisotropy across the caldera
figures.caption: All six stations pooled, each measurement assigned to its ray's arc-length lateral midpoint on a 0.25 × 0.25 km grid, minimum 10 measurements per cell, one row × seven periods. Fractional anisotropy solved from a² + 2xa − 4 = 0 with x = 2·T_travel/δt. Note that AXEC2's 2015–2021 half lacks event coordinates, so only its 2022–2026 data contributes.

figures.title: Fast direction across the caldera
figures.caption: The fast-direction quiver companion to the panel above, on the same grid and periods.

figures.title: Percent anisotropy through time — AXEC3
figures.caption: φ against time in 21-day windows with a ±24 h eruption zoom, and δt/T_travel × 100 against time.

figures.title: Inverted anisotropy strength
figures.caption: Joint six-station 2-D inversion, one row × seven equal-inflation periods. Quad-tree blocks to a 0.25 km minimum, d = Gm with δt_r = Σ s_b L_rb, Sherman–Morrison covariance whitening, bounded weighted least squares. Blocks failing checkerboard recovery are greyed and hatched.

figures.title: Inverted fast direction
figures.caption: Per-block fast polarisation from the same inversion, averaged in doubled-angle space.

figures.title: Checkerboard resolution test
figures.caption: Input against recovered checkerboard, λ = 1 km, joint six-station, Q_w ≥ 0.7. From the July 2026 run — the Grade-3 inversion produced strength and quiver output but no checkerboard, so this stands in until that is regenerated.

figures.title: How well does each DMODELS scenario fit?
figures.caption: Left: each grid's modeled principal-compression azimuth against the Grade-3 fast direction for its own period (pre grids vs pre-eruption, syn grids vs syn-eruption), RMS over six stations. Right: every pre → syn pair scored on the predicted CHANGE in azimuth, RMS about the 1:1 line. The dotted line is 52°, the RMS of a random axial misfit — the change test lands on or beyond it for every pair.

figures.title: Pre-1 → Syn-6: change in stress and fast direction
figures.caption: Baillard's change comparison, re-run on Grade-3 observations. Left: modeled change in σ₁ − σ₂ against observed change in median δt (10 ms quantisation is visible). Right: modeled vs observed change in azimuth against the 1:1 line — observed rotation is clockwise at every station, modeled is mixed.

figures.title: Syn-6 — modeled maximum compressive stress axis
figures.caption: Horizontal displacement magnitude with the most compressive horizontal stress axis, Syn-6 (dikes + prolate spheroid). Colormap carried over unchanged from Baillard's original plotting code.

figures.title: Pre-1 — modeled maximum compressive stress axis
figures.caption: As above, for the best-fitting pre-eruption scenario.

figures.title: Syn-5 — model vs observed at each station
figures.caption: Best syn-eruption grid by azimuth RMS (29°). Left: modeled σ₁ − σ₂ vs observed δt with linear fit. Right: modeled vs observed azimuth, 180°-wrapped.

figures.title: Syn-6 — model vs observed at each station
figures.caption: Second-best syn grid (33°); the stress–δt fit is flat (slope ≈ 0).

figures.title: Pre-1 — model vs observed at each station
figures.caption: Best pre-eruption grid (37° vs 54° for Pre-2).
